name: QLever
tagline: Fast open-source SPARQL engine that serves all of Wikidata or OpenStreetMap from one machine.
description: QLever is an open-source SPARQL engine from the University of Freiburg's algorithms group, written in C++ and designed to load and query very large RDF datasets (full Wikidata, UniProt, OpenStreetMap, PubChem) on a single commodity server. It builds compressed, sorted index permutations ahead of time and adds text search over literals and GeoSPARQL-style spatial queries, often answering complex queries in well under a second where older triplestores time out. SPARQL Update support has landed recently. It is the leading candidate for heavy read-mostly public endpoints, but it is still pre-1.0 and has no clustering.
developer: University of Freiburg (Chair of Algorithms and Data Structures)

scale.notes: Tens of billions of triples (full Wikidata and larger) on one machine with fast SSDs.

strengths: Loads and queries full Wikidata-scale datasets on a single commodity machine
Complex SPARQL queries often finish in sub-second time where other engines time out
Built-in text search and spatial predicates over OpenStreetMap-style data
Simple qlever CLI automates download, indexing and serving
weaknesses: Pre-1.0: SPARQL Update and some features are still maturing
Index builds are offline and take hours for the largest datasets
No clustering, replication or access control built in
useCases: Public SPARQL endpoints for Wikidata, OSM, UniProt
